bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to natural resources; providing for fraud prevention in registrations, licenses, passes, and permits issued by the commissioner; providing criminal penalties; amending Minnesota Statutes 2024, sections 84.82, by adding a subdivision; 84.8205, by adding a subdivision; 85.053, by adding a subdivision; 97A.311, subdivisions 1, 2, by adding a subdivision; proposing coding for new law in Minnesota Statutes, chapters 84; 85; 86B.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.

[84.7885] UNLAWFUL ACTS RELATED TO REGISTRATION.

Subdivision 1.

Violations.

With regard to any registration or temporary registration issued under section 84.788, it is unlawful for any person or dealer:

(1) to issue, obtain, or use a dealer temporary 21-day registration permit without the intent to follow through with a sale and registration;

(2) to obtain, attempt to obtain, or assist in obtaining a registration through misrepresentation or fraud by knowingly providing incorrect, misleading, incomplete, or materially untrue information in the registration application; or

(3) to display, cause or permit to be displayed, or have in possession any fictitious or fraudulent registration or decal.

Subd. 2.

Penalties.

(a) A dealer temporary 21-day registration permit, registration, or registration sticker that is the subject of a violation under subdivision 1 is void.

(b) A person who violates subdivision 1 is guilty of a misdemeanor.

(c) A dealer who violates subdivision 1 is guilty of a gross misdemeanor.

Sec. 2.

[84.7985] UNLAWFUL ACTS RELATED TO REGISTRATION.

Subdivision 1.

Violations.

With regard to any registration or temporary registration issued under section 84.798, it is unlawful for any person or dealer:

(1) to issue, obtain, or use a dealer temporary 21-day registration permit without the intent to follow through with a sale and registration;

(2) to obtain, attempt to obtain, or assist in obtaining a registration through misrepresentation or fraud by knowingly providing incorrect, misleading, incomplete, or materially untrue information in the registration application; or

(3) to display, cause or permit to be displayed, or have in possession any fictitious or fraudulent registration or decal.

Subd. 2.

Penalties.

(a) A dealer temporary 21-day registration permit, registration, or registration sticker that is the subject of a violation under subdivision 1 is void.

(b) A person who violates subdivision 1 is guilty of a misdemeanor.

(c) A dealer who violates subdivision 1 is guilty of a gross misdemeanor.

Sec. 3.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 84.82, is amended by adding a subdivision to read:

Subd. 12.

Unlawful acts related to registration.

(a) It is unlawful for any person:

(1) to issue, obtain, or use a dealer temporary 21-day registration permit without the intent to follow through with a sale and registration;

(2) to register or attempt to register a snowmobile through misrepresentation or fraud by knowingly providing incorrect, misleading, incomplete, or materially untrue information in the registration application; or

(3) to display, cause or permit to be displayed, or have in possession any fictitious or fraudulent registration or decal.

(b) A dealer temporary 21-day registration permit, registration, or decal that is the subject of a violation under paragraph (a) is void.

(c) A person who violates paragraph (a) is guilty of a misdemeanor.

(d) A dealer who violates paragraph (a) is guilty of a gross misdemeanor.

Sec. 4.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 84.8205, is amended by adding a subdivision to read:

Subd. 7.

Penalties.

A person who makes a false statement related to an application for a snowmobile state trail pass, materially alters or creates a fictitious snowmobile state trail pass, or uses or attempts to use a materially altered, fictitious, or otherwise fraudulent snowmobile state trail pass is guilty of a misdemeanor, and the pass is rendered void.

Sec. 5.

[84.9225] UNLAWFUL ACTS RELATED TO REGISTRATION.

Subdivision 1.

Violations.

With regard to any registration or temporary registration issued under section 84.922, it is unlawful for any person or dealer:

(1) to issue, obtain, or use a dealer temporary 21-day registration permit without the intent to follow through with a sale and registration;

(2) to obtain, attempt to obtain, or assist in obtaining a registration through misrepresentation or fraud by knowingly providing incorrect, misleading, incomplete, or materially untrue information in the registration application; or

(3) to display, cause or permit to be displayed, or have in possession any fictitious or fraudulent registration or decal.

Subd. 2.

Penalties.

(a) A dealer temporary 21-day registration permit, registration, or registration sticker that is the subject of a violation under subdivision 1 is void.

(b) A person who violates subdivision 1 is guilty of a misdemeanor.

(c) A dealer who violates subdivision 1 is guilty of a gross misdemeanor.

Sec. 6.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 85.053, is amended by adding a subdivision to read:

Subd. 11.

Penalties.

A person who makes a false statement related to an application for a state park permit, materially alters or creates a fictitious state park permit, or uses or attempts to use a materially altered, fictitious, or otherwise fraudulent state park permit is guilty of a misdemeanor, and the permit is void.

Sec. 7.

[85.48] PENALTIES; FALSE STATEMENTS OR ALTERATIONS.

Subdivision 1.

False statement.

A person who makes a false statement related to an application for a cross-country-ski pass or a horse pass is guilty of a misdemeanor, and the pass is void.

Subd. 2.

Altered or fictitious pass.

A person who materially alters or creates a fictitious cross-country-ski pass or horse pass or uses or attempts to use a materially altered, fictitious, or otherwise fraudulent cross-country-ski pass or horse pass is guilty of a misdemeanor, and the pass is void.

Sec. 8.

[86B.425] UNLAWFUL ACTS RELATED TO LICENSE.

Subdivision 1.

Violations.

With regard to any license issued under section 86B.401, 86B.405, or 86B.411, it is unlawful for any person or dealer:

(1) to issue, obtain, or use a temporary license certificate without the intent to follow through with the license application and sale;

(2) to obtain or attempt to obtain a license or registration sticker through misrepresentation or fraud by knowingly providing incorrect, misleading, incomplete, or materially untrue information in the license application; or

(3) to display, cause or permit to be displayed, or have in possession any fictitious or fraudulent license or registration sticker.

Subd. 2.

Penalties.

(a) A temporary license certificate, license, or registration sticker that is the subject of a violation under subdivision 1 is void.

(b) A person who violates subdivision 1 is guilty of a misdemeanor.

(c) A dealer who violates subdivision 1 is guilty of a gross misdemeanor.

Sec. 9.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 97A.311, subdivision 1, is amended to read:

Subdivision 1.
Fictitious or altered license or permit.
A person that alters a license or permit in a material manner, creates a fictitious license or permit, buys or sells a fictitious or materially altered license or permit, or uses or attempts to use a materially altered, fictitious, or otherwise fraudulent license or permit is guilty of a misdemeanor and subject to the penalties in subdivision 7.

Sec. 10.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 97A.311, subdivision 2, is amended to read:

Subd. 2.
False statement.
A person that knowingly makes a false statement related to an application for a license or permit or related to a license, permit, or certificate required by or issued under the game and fish laws is guilty of a misdemeanor and subject to the penalties in subdivision 7.

Sec. 11.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 97A.311, is amended by adding a subdivision to read:

Subd. 7.

Penalties.

A license or permit that is the subject of a violation under subdivision 1 or 2 is void, and the person convicted of violating subdivision 1 or 2 is subject to the following penalties:

(1) upon first conviction, the person may not obtain a license or permit of that type for one year;

(2) upon second conviction, all the person's licenses to take wild animals are void and the person may not obtain a license to take a wild animal or a permit of that type for one year; and

(3) upon third conviction, all the person's licenses to take wild animals are void and the person may not obtain a license to take a wild animal or a permit of that type for five years.

bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to natural resources; providing for fraud prevention in registrations, licenses, passes, and permits issued by the commissioner; providing criminal penalties; amending Minnesota Statutes 2024, sections 84.82, by adding a subdivision; 84.8205, by adding a subdivision; 85.053, by adding a subdivision; 97A.311, subdivisions 1, 2, by adding a subdivision; proposing coding for new law in Minnesota Statutes, chapters 84; 85; 86B.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.

[84.7885] UNLAWFUL ACTS RELATED TO REGISTRATION.

Subdivision 1.

Violations.

With regard to any registration or temporary registration issued under section 84.788, it is unlawful for any person or dealer:

(1) to issue, obtain, or use a dealer temporary 21-day registration permit without the intent to follow through with a sale and registration;

(2) to obtain, attempt to obtain, or assist in obtaining a registration through misrepresentation or fraud by knowingly providing incorrect, misleading, incomplete, or materially untrue information in the registration application; or

(3) to display, cause or permit to be displayed, or have in possession any fictitious or fraudulent registration or decal.

Subd. 2.

Penalties.

(a) A dealer temporary 21-day registration permit, registration, or registration sticker that is the subject of a violation under subdivision 1 is void.

(b) A person who violates subdivision 1 is guilty of a misdemeanor.

(c) A dealer who violates subdivision 1 is guilty of a gross misdemeanor.

Sec. 2.

[84.7985] UNLAWFUL ACTS RELATED TO REGISTRATION.

Subdivision 1.

Violations.

With regard to any registration or temporary registration issued under section 84.798, it is unlawful for any person or dealer:

(1) to issue, obtain, or use a dealer temporary 21-day registration permit without the intent to follow through with a sale and registration;

(2) to obtain, attempt to obtain, or assist in obtaining a registration through misrepresentation or fraud by knowingly providing incorrect, misleading, incomplete, or materially untrue information in the registration application; or

(3) to display, cause or permit to be displayed, or have in possession any fictitious or fraudulent registration or decal.

Subd. 2.

Penalties.

(a) A dealer temporary 21-day registration permit, registration, or registration sticker that is the subject of a violation under subdivision 1 is void.

(b) A person who violates subdivision 1 is guilty of a misdemeanor.

(c) A dealer who violates subdivision 1 is guilty of a gross misdemeanor.

Sec. 3.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 84.82, is amended by adding a subdivision to read:

Subd. 12.

Unlawful acts related to registration.

(a) It is unlawful for any person:

(1) to issue, obtain, or use a dealer temporary 21-day registration permit without the intent to follow through with a sale and registration;

(2) to register or attempt to register a snowmobile through misrepresentation or fraud by knowingly providing incorrect, misleading, incomplete, or materially untrue information in the registration application; or

(3) to display, cause or permit to be displayed, or have in possession any fictitious or fraudulent registration or decal.

(b) A dealer temporary 21-day registration permit, registration, or decal that is the subject of a violation under paragraph (a) is void.

(c) A person who violates paragraph (a) is guilty of a misdemeanor.

(d) A dealer who violates paragraph (a) is guilty of a gross misdemeanor.

Sec. 4.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 84.8205, is amended by adding a subdivision to read:

Subd. 7.

Penalties.

A person who makes a false statement related to an application for a snowmobile state trail pass, materially alters or creates a fictitious snowmobile state trail pass, or uses or attempts to use a materially altered, fictitious, or otherwise fraudulent snowmobile state trail pass is guilty of a misdemeanor, and the pass is rendered void.

Sec. 5.

[84.9225] UNLAWFUL ACTS RELATED TO REGISTRATION.

Subdivision 1.

Violations.

With regard to any registration or temporary registration issued under section 84.922, it is unlawful for any person or dealer:

(1) to issue, obtain, or use a dealer temporary 21-day registration permit without the intent to follow through with a sale and registration;

(2) to obtain, attempt to obtain, or assist in obtaining a registration through misrepresentation or fraud by knowingly providing incorrect, misleading, incomplete, or materially untrue information in the registration application; or

(3) to display, cause or permit to be displayed, or have in possession any fictitious or fraudulent registration or decal.

Subd. 2.

Penalties.

(a) A dealer temporary 21-day registration permit, registration, or registration sticker that is the subject of a violation under subdivision 1 is void.

(b) A person who violates subdivision 1 is guilty of a misdemeanor.

(c) A dealer who violates subdivision 1 is guilty of a gross misdemeanor.

Sec. 6.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 85.053, is amended by adding a subdivision to read:

Subd. 11.

Penalties.

A person who makes a false statement related to an application for a state park permit, materially alters or creates a fictitious state park permit, or uses or attempts to use a materially altered, fictitious, or otherwise fraudulent state park permit is guilty of a misdemeanor, and the permit is void.

Sec. 7.

[85.48] PENALTIES; FALSE STATEMENTS OR ALTERATIONS.

Subdivision 1.

False statement.

A person who makes a false statement related to an application for a cross-country-ski pass or a horse pass is guilty of a misdemeanor, and the pass is void.

Subd. 2.

Altered or fictitious pass.

A person who materially alters or creates a fictitious cross-country-ski pass or horse pass or uses or attempts to use a materially altered, fictitious, or otherwise fraudulent cross-country-ski pass or horse pass is guilty of a misdemeanor, and the pass is void.

Sec. 8.

[86B.425] UNLAWFUL ACTS RELATED TO LICENSE.

Subdivision 1.

Violations.

With regard to any license issued under section 86B.401, 86B.405, or 86B.411, it is unlawful for any person or dealer:

(1) to issue, obtain, or use a temporary license certificate without the intent to follow through with the license application and sale;

(2) to obtain or attempt to obtain a license or registration sticker through misrepresentation or fraud by knowingly providing incorrect, misleading, incomplete, or materially untrue information in the license application; or

(3) to display, cause or permit to be displayed, or have in possession any fictitious or fraudulent license or registration sticker.

Subd. 2.

Penalties.

(a) A temporary license certificate, license, or registration sticker that is the subject of a violation under subdivision 1 is void.

(b) A person who violates subdivision 1 is guilty of a misdemeanor.

(c) A dealer who violates subdivision 1 is guilty of a gross misdemeanor.

Sec. 9.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 97A.311, subdivision 1, is amended to read:

Subdivision 1.
Fictitious or altered license or permit.
A person that alters a license or permit in a material manner, creates a fictitious license or permit, buys or sells a fictitious or materially altered license or permit, or uses or attempts to use a materially altered, fictitious, or otherwise fraudulent license or permit is guilty of a misdemeanor and subject to the penalties in subdivision 7.

Sec. 10.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 97A.311, subdivision 2, is amended to read:

Subd. 2.
False statement.
A person that knowingly makes a false statement related to an application for a license or permit or related to a license, permit, or certificate required by or issued under the game and fish laws is guilty of a misdemeanor and subject to the penalties in subdivision 7.

Sec. 11.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 97A.311, is amended by adding a subdivision to read:

Subd. 7.

Penalties.

A license or permit that is the subject of a violation under subdivision 1 or 2 is void, and the person convicted of violating subdivision 1 or 2 is subject to the following penalties:

(1) upon first conviction, the person may not obtain a license or permit of that type for one year;

(2) upon second conviction, all the person's licenses to take wild animals are void and the person may not obtain a license to take a wild animal or a permit of that type for one year; and

(3) upon third conviction, all the person's licenses to take wild animals are void and the person may not obtain a license to take a wild animal or a permit of that type for five years.
